25.title: Natural Madd with Alif (Madd Tabee'ee)
25.desc: A silent Alif preceded by a letter with Fatha. It is stretched smoothly for exactly 2 beats (Natural Madd).
25.html: بَـ + ا = بَـا • قَـالَ

25.title: Alif Madd Application (Madd Tabee'ee)
25.desc: Prolong the Fatha sound for 2 counts without cutting or overextending.
25.html: ءَادَمُ • هَاجَرَ • طَاقَةَ

27.title: Dagger Alif Madd (Alif Khanjariyya)
27.desc: A small superscript Alif (ٰ) in Quranic script. It functions exactly like a full Madd Alif and takes 2 beats.
27.html: بَـا = بَـٰ • مَـٰلِكِ

27.title: Dagger Alif Positions (Alif Khanjariyya)
27.desc: It can be written directly above a letter, over a dotless Yaa (ـىٰ), or over a Waw (ـوٰ).
27.html: سَـىٰ • نَـوٰ • إِلَـىٰ • ذَٰلِكَ

28.title: Natural Madd with Yaa (Madd Tabee'ee)
28.desc: A silent Yaa preceded by a letter with Kasra. It stretches the Kasra sound for exactly 2 beats.
28.html: بِـ + ى = بِـى • قِـيـلَ

28.title: Short Kasra vs Madd Yaa (Phonetic Contrast)
28.desc: Contrast the 1-beat short Kasra against the 2-beat elongated Madd Yaa.
28.html: إِ ⟷ إِى • دِ ⟷ دِى

31.title: Small Yaa Connection (Mad Silah Sughra)
31.desc: Connecting Haa of pronoun with a small Yaa (ۦ) prolonged for 2 beats when between two voweled letters.
31.html: هِى = ـهِۦ = هِۦ

31.title: Small Yaa Script Behavior (Yaa Saghirah)
31.desc: The small Yaa in Quranic script behaves exactly like a regular Madd Yaa.
31.html:
يِ = ۦِ =
يَ = ۦَ

32.title: Short Vowels (Harakat: 1 Beat)
32.desc: Fatha, Kasra, and Damma are short vowels. They take exactly 1 beat.
32.html: بَ - بِ - بُ

32.title: Long Vowels (Madd Letters: 2 Beats)
32.desc: Alif, Yaa, and Waw are Madd letters. They stretch the sound to 2 beats.
32.html: بَا - بِي - بُو

33.title: Natural Madd with Waw (Madd Tabee'ee)
33.desc: A silent Waw preceded by a letter with Damma. It is stretched smoothly for 2 beats.
33.html: بُـ + و = بُـو • يَـقُـولُ

33.title: Short Damma vs Madd Waw (Phonetic Contrast)
33.desc: Prolong the Damma sound for 2 counts to generate the long Madd Waw sound.
33.html: صُمِ ⟷ صُـومِى • قُلِ ⟷ قُـولِى

35.title: Small Waw Connection (Mad Silah Sughra)
35.desc: Connecting Haa of pronoun with a small Waw (ۥ) prolonged for 2 beats when situated between two voweled letters.
35.html: هُو = ـهُۥ = هُۥ

35.title: Small Waw Script Behavior (Waw Saghirah)
35.desc: The small subscript Waw in Quranic orthography behaves like a standard Madd Waw.
35.html: دَاوُۥدُ • وُۥرِىَ • لَهُۥ

39.title: Quranic Sukun Symbol (Ras Khaa)
39.desc: Marked by a small headless Khaa (ۡ) above the letter, denoting clear and distinct pronunciation (Izhar).
39.html: أَبۡ • أَتۡ • أَثۡ • أَجۡ

39.title: Pronunciation of Sukun (Silent Letters)
39.desc: A silent letter cannot be initiated alone; it must be pronounced coupled with the preceding voweled letter.
39.html: بَـ + حۡ = بَحۡ

42.title: Definite Moon Lam (Lam Qamariyyah)
42.desc: An extra Lam that is written and pronounced clearly. Marked in Quranic script with a Sukun (ۡ) over the Lam.
42.html: ٱلۡـبَلَدِ • ٱلۡـأَمِينِ • ٱلۡـمَلِكُ

42.title: Moon Lam 14 Letters (Huroof Qamariyyah)
42.desc: Followed by 14 specific letters grouped in: (اِبۡغِ حَجَّكَ وَخَفۡ عَقِيمَهُ).
42.html: ٱلۡـأَتۡقَىٰ • ٱلۡـبُرُوجِ • ٱلۡـغَاوُونَ

50.title: Double Fatha Tanween (Tanween Fath)
50.desc: An extra unwritten silent Noon pronounced in continuity, written as double Fatha (ً) with an appended Alif.
50.html: بَـنۡ = بًا • دَنۡ = دًا

50.title: Exceptions to Appended Alif (Tanween Fath)
50.desc: No Alif is added after Taa Marbutah (ـةً), Hamza preceded by Alif (ـاءً), or Alif Maqsurah (ـدًى).
50.html: رَحۡمَةً • مَآءً • هُدًى

53.title: Double Kasra Tanween (Tanween Kasr)
53.desc: An extra unwritten silent Noon pronounced in continuity, written as double Kasra (ٍ) beneath the letter.
53.html: تِـنۡ = تٍ • جِـنۡ = جٍ

53.title: Pronunciation of Tanween Kasr
53.desc: Pronounced like a Kasra-voweled letter immediately followed by a silent Noon sound.
53.html: عَمَلٍ • رَسُولٍ • يَوۡمٍ

56.title: Double Damma Tanween (Tanween Damm)
56.desc: An extra unwritten silent Noon pronounced in continuity, written as double Damma (ٌ) above the letter.
56.html: ثُـنۡ = ثٌ • خُـنۡ = خٌ

56.title: Pronunciation of Tanween Damm
56.desc: Pronounced like a Damma-voweled letter immediately followed by a silent Noon sound.
56.html: عَلِيمٌ • حَكِيمٌ • سَمِيعٌ

62.title: Doubled Letter with Fatha (Shaddah bi-Fath)
62.desc: Two identical letters merged into one: the first is silent and the second is voweled with Fatha.
62.html: بَدۡدَ = بَدَّ • وَفۡفَ = وَفَّ

62.title: Shaddah with Fatha and Madd Alif
62.desc: Hold on the silent letter first, then prolong the second Fatha-voweled letter for 2 beats.
62.html: فَـصَّـا • تَـوَّابًا • غَـفَّارًا

64.title: Definite Sun Lam (Lam Shamsiyyah)
64.desc: An extra Lam that is written but not pronounced, merging fully into the following letter marked with Shaddah.
64.html: ٱلـشَّـمۡسُ • ٱلـنَّـاسُ • ٱلـرَّحۡمَـٰنُ

64.title: Sun Lam 14 Letters (Huroof Shamsiyyah)
64.desc: Followed by 14 specific letters: (ط، ث، ص، ر، ت، ض، ذ، ن، د، س، ظ، ز، ش، ل).
64.html: ٱلـطَّـارِقِ • ٱلـثَّـوَّابُ • ٱلـصَّـاعِقَةُ

66.title: Doubled Letter with Kasra (Shaddah bi-Kasr)
66.desc: Merges a silent letter into a Kasra-voweled letter; the Kasra sign is placed beneath the Shaddah.
66.html: رَبۡـبِ = رَبِّ • عَفۡـفِ = عَفِّ

66.title: Shaddah with Kasra and Madd Yaa
66.desc: Hold on the doubled letter with Kasra and stretch for 2 beats into the long Madd Yaa.
66.html: أَذِّى • جَدِّى • ذُرِّيَّةً

70.title: Doubled Letter with Damma (Shaddah bi-Damm)
70.desc: Merges a silent letter into a Damma-voweled letter; the Damma sign is placed above the Shaddah.
70.html: أُفۡـفُ = أُفُّ • عَدۡدُ = عَدُّ

70.title: Shaddah with Damma and Madd Waw
70.desc: Hold on the doubled letter with Damma and stretch for 2 beats into the long Madd Waw.
70.html: عَدُّو • يَـظُـنُّونَ • يَـمُـدُّونَ

75.title: Doubled Letter with Tanween (Shaddah with Tanween)
75.desc: Combines letter doubling (Shaddah) with Tanween (Fath, Kasr, or Damm) on the same letter.
75.html: أَبًّا • فَكٍّ • صَبٌّ

75.title: Pronunciation of Shaddah with Tanween
75.desc: Apply firm pressure on the doubled letter's articulation point, then articulate the silent Noon of Tanween.
75.html: حَـظًّا • غَـضٍّ • حَـقٌّ

77.title: Mandatory Connected Madd (Madd Muttasil)
77.desc: When a Madd letter is followed by a Hamza within the same word. Stretched for 4 or 5 beats.
77.html: جَآءَ • الـسُّوٓءَ • حُنَفَآءَ

77.title: Permissible Separated Madd (Madd Munfasil)
77.desc: When a Madd letter ends a word and Hamza begins the next word. Stretched for 4 or 5 beats.
77.html: إِذَآ [أَصَابَتۡهُم] • وَمَآ [أُمِرُوٓاْ]

77.title: Substituted Madd (Madd Badal)
77.desc: When a Hamza precedes the Madd letter within a single word. Stretched for 2 beats.
77.html: ءَامَنُواْ • أُوتُواْ • إِيمَـٰنًا

78.title: Temporary Stopping Madd (Madd Aarid & Leen)
78.desc: When pausing causes the letter after a Madd or Leen letter to become temporarily silent (2, 4, or 6 beats).
78.html: نَسۡتَعِيـنُ • الْـبَيۡتِ • خَوۡفٍ

78.title: Compulsory Word Madd (Madd Lazim Kalimi)
78.desc: When a permanent Sukun or Shaddah follows a Madd letter within a word. Must be stretched for 6 full beats.
78.html: الـضَّـآلِّيـنَ • الْـحَآقَّةُ • ءَآلۡـَٔـٰنَ

78.title: Compulsory Letter Madd (Madd Lazim Harfi)
78.desc: Occurs in disjointed Surah opening letters (نَقَصَ عَسَلُكُمْ). Must be stretched for 6 full beats.
78.html: الٓمٓ • كهيعٓصٓ • حمٓ عٓسٓقٓ

80.title: Throat Clear Pronunciation (Izhar Halqi)
80.desc: Pronounce silent Noon or Tanween clearly without Ghunnah before the 6 throat letters: (ء، هـ، ع، ح، غ، خ).
80.html: مَنۡ ءَامَنَ • يَنۡهَوۡنَ • مِيثَـٰقًا غَلِيـظًا

80.title: Merging with Nasalization (Idgham bi-Ghunnah)
80.desc: Merge silent Noon or Tanween into (ي، ن، م، و) with a 2-beat nasal resonance (Ghunnah).
80.html: مَن يَّقُولُ • مَالًا مَّمۡدُودًا • خَيۡرٌ نُّزُلًا

80.title: Complete Merging without Ghunnah (Idgham bila-Ghunnah)
80.desc: Merge silent Noon or Tanween completely into (ل، ر) without nasalization.
80.html: مِن رَّحِيمٍ • وَمَن لَّمۡ • مَالًا لُّبَدًا

81.title: Conversion to Meem (Iqlab)
81.desc: Convert silent Noon or Tanween into a concealed Meem with Ghunnah when followed by Baa (marked by ۢ).
81.html: مِنۢ بَعۡدِ • مُنۢبَثًّا • عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ

81.title: True Concealment (Ikhfa Haqiqi)
81.desc: Conceal silent Noon or Tanween between Izhar and Idgham with Ghunnah before 15 specific letters.
81.html: مِن قَـبۡلُ • أَنتُمۡ • شَجَرَةٍ تَخۡرُجُ

81.title: Absolute Manifestation (Izhar Mutlaq)
81.desc: Mandatory clear pronunciation when silent Noon meets an Idgham letter in a single word (دُنۡيَا، بُنۡيَـٰنٌ، قِنۡوَانٌ، صِنۡوَانٌ).
81.html: دُنۡيَا • بُنۡيَـٰنٌ • قِنۡوَانٌ

83.title: Labial Concealment (Ikhfa Shafawi)
83.desc: Conceal silent Meem with a 2-beat Ghunnah when followed immediately by the letter Baa.
83.html: تَرۡمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ • هُم بِهِۦ

83.title: Identical Meem Merging (Idgham Mithlayn Saghir)
83.desc: Merge silent Meem into a following voweled Meem with a 2-beat Ghunnah.
83.html: لَهُم مَّا يَشَاءُونَ • كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ

83.title: Labial Clarity (Izhar Shafawi)
83.desc: Pronounce silent Meem clearly without Ghunnah before the other 26 letters (especially Waw and Faa).
83.html: لَمۡ يَـلِدۡ • عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا • هُمۡ فِيهَا

83.title: Doubled Noon & Meem Ghunnah
83.desc: Mandatory 2-beat clear nasalization (Ghunnah) on doubled Noon (نّ) and doubled Meem (مّ) in continuity and stopping.
83.html: إِنَّ • ثُمَّ • الـنَّـاسِ

85.title: Identical Letters Merging (Idgham Mutamathilayn)
85.desc: When two identical letters meet where the first is silent and the second is voweled, merge fully into the second.
85.html: ٱضۡرِب بِّعَصَاكَ • بَل لَّجُّواْ • يُدۡرِككُّمُ

85.title: Close Letters Merging (Idgham Mutaqaribayn)
85.desc: When two letters close in articulation point and attributes meet with the first silent (e.g. Lam into Raa, Qaf into Kaf).
85.html: وَقُل رَّبِّ • أَلَمۡ نَخۡلُقكُّم

85.title: Homogeneous Letters Merging (Idgham Mutajanisayn)
85.desc: When two letters share articulation point but differ in attributes (e.g. Taa into Taa/Daal, Dhal into Zhaa, Baa into Meem).
85.html: قَد تَّبَيَّنَ • أَثۡقَلَت دَّعَوَا • يَـٰبُنَيَّ ٱرۡكَب مَّعَنَا

86.title: Echoing Consonants (Qalqalah)
86.desc: A rhythmic bouncing echo when pronouncing the 5 silent letters of (قَطۡبُ جَدٍّ).
86.html: ٱقۡتَرَبَ • فَوَسَطۡنَ • أَجۡدَرُ • يَبۡحَثُ • يُدۡخِلُ

86.title: Rules of Letter Raa (Tafkheem & Tarqeeq)
86.desc: Raa is heavy (Tafkheem) with Fatha/Damma or after them; it is light (Tarqeeq) with Kasra or after an original Kasra.
86.html: رَحۡمَةً • رُسُلًا • رِزۡقًا • فِرۡعَوۡنَ

86.title: Connecting Hamza (Hamzat Wasl)
86.desc: Pronounced at the start of speech and dropped in continuity; starts with Fatha on (Al), Damma on third letter Damma, and Kasra otherwise.
86.html: ٱلۡـحَمۡدُ • ٱدۡعُ • ٱهۡدِنَا • ٱبۡنَ

89.title: Quranic vs Standard Sukun (Orthography Differences)
89.desc: Quranic Sukun is shaped as a headless Khaa (ۡ) signifying clarity, whereas standard dictation uses a circle (ْ).
89.html: فِعۡلَ [Quranic] ⟷ فِعْلَ [Standard]

89.title: Quranic vs Standard Tanween (Orthography Differences)
89.desc: Quranic Tanween marks pronunciation rules (parallel for Izhar, sequential for Idgham/Ikhfa, Meem for Iqlab).
89.html: عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ • سَمِيعُۢ بَصِيرٌ

89.title: Connecting Alif & Madd Signs (Orthography Differences)
89.desc: Marked by a miniature Saad (ٱ) for Hamzat Wasl and an authentic tilde wave (ٓ) for prolonged Madd.
89.html: ٱلۡـمَلِكُ • بِمَآ أُنزِلَ

90.title: Spoken Letters Omitted in Dictation
90.desc: Alif is pronounced but omitted in standard writing in specific words (هذا, ذلك, الله, الرحمن), while preserved as dagger Alif (ٰ) in Quranic script.
90.html: هَـٰذَا [Quranic] ⟷ هَذَا [Standard]

90.title: Dagger Alif Pronunciation in Quran
90.desc: Behaves exactly like a standard full-length Madd Alif, stretched for 2 full counts in recitation.
90.html: ذَٰلِكَ • هَـٰؤُلَاءِ • الـرَّحۡمَـٰنِ

91.title: Medial Hamza on Nabrah / Yaa (Hamza Mutawassitah)
91.desc: Written on a Nabrah (seat) if the Hamza is with Kasra, or preceded by Kasra or a silent Yaa.
91.html: سُئِلَ • يَوۡمَئِذٍ • خَـٰطِئِينَ

91.title: Medial Hamza on Waw (Hamza Mutawassitah)
91.desc: Written on Waw if the Hamza has Damma (and not preceded by Kasra), or is silent preceded by Damma.
91.html: مُؤۡمِنُونَ • يَؤُوسٌ • تَـفَـٰؤُلٌ

92.title: Medial Hamza on Baseline (Hamza on Line)
92.desc: Written standalone on the baseline when it has Fatha following a silent Madd Alif or Madd Waw.
92.html: تَـفَـٰءَلَ • تَـسَـٰءَلُواْ • مَـرُوٓءَةً

92.title: Terminal Hamza (Hamza Mutatarriqah)
92.desc: Written matching the preceding vowel: on Alif after Fatha, on Yaa after Kasra, on Waw after Damma, on line after Sukun.
92.html: قَرَأَ • شَـٰطِئ • تَـبَاطُؤ • الـنِّسَآءَ
